item.title: Paul Finebaum calls out Oklahoma AD Roger Denny for ‘pandering’ after Ole Miss game move
item.description: Paul Finebaum went after Oklahoma athletic director Roger Denny on SEC Network on Saturday morning, hours after Denny publicly objected to the SEC moving the Sooners’ game against the Ole Miss Rebels to Sunday. Speaking with Matt Barrie, Finebaum defended Commissioner Greg Sankey and then turned the conversation toward Denny’s first year in charge in Norman. Denny’s statement, posted around midnight, said Sankey moved the game over Oklahoma’s strong objection and warned that refusing to play at the new time would mean a forfeit. Dec 7, 2024; Atlanta, GA, USA; ESPN announcer Paul Finebaum before the 2024 SEC Championship game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images “First of all, I understand the frustration, and none of us really know what happened to Ole Miss, but I believe the administration at Ole Miss did everything they could. What I don’t think is correct is Roger Denny, the athletic director there, pathetically pandering to his fan base at midnight to try to cover up whatever, I don’t know. But Mr. Sankey, the commissioner of the Southeastern Conference, made a decision for the entire conference and for the safety of everyone. He’s not concerned about what you’re doing with your fan base, and what Roger Denny has been doing all year is pandering to his fan base. Before the season, Matt, he gave his football coach Brent Venables a contract extension. They were ranked number nine in the country. They have now lost four games and are out of the playoffs. Why did he do that? Because he’s an impulsive leader. He’s a former tax attorney. I’m not castigating tax attorneys or attorneys in general, but they run differently. And what he did here is really against the code of the SEC, to call out a commissioner during a national crisis and emergency. He’s thinking about himself and his fan base, who was already on tenterhooks because of the season, and I think he is dead wrong. And quite frankly, I think it’s unbecoming of a leader in college athletics or anywhere to do what he did,” Finebaum said. Paul Finebaum criticized Oklahoma AD Roger Denny for a midnight statement where he blasted the SEC’s decision to move the Ole Miss game to Sunday. https://t.co/MOmFA4SGk2 — Sports Fountain (@sportfountain) November 14, 2026 Denny announced Venables’ two-year extension on Aug. 20, two weeks before the opener, with Oklahoma ranked No. 9 in the preseason coaches poll and No. 10 by the AP. The new six-year contract runs through 2031 and is worth about $63 million. The Sooners take a 5-4 record into Sunday. Denny is a tax lawyer by training who spent nearly 15 years as a corporate attorney before moving into athletics administration at Illinois, and he took over at Oklahoma in February. When Paul Finebaum started questioning Roger Denny’s judgment Finebaum first tied Venables’ struggles to Denny in late September. After Oklahoma lost at Georgia, he went on The Matt Barrie Show and put the extension squarely on the athletic director.

item.title: Jaguars Arik Armstead fined for hip-drop tackle vs. Ravens in Week 9
item.description: Photo by Don Juan Moore/Getty Images | Getty Images Arik Armstead will be fined $17,911 for a hip-drop tackle in the Jaguars’ Week 9 win over the Baltimore Ravens. The fine for unnecessary roughness stems from a tackle on Derrick Henry on the Ravens’ very first offensive play of the third quarter. The play was a direct snap to Henry, who was stopped after just 1 yard by Armstead and Matt Dickerson. Armstead was not flagged for the play at the time. The fine is Armstead’s second of the season, after being fined 11,941 for a face mask penalty when the Jaguars played the Patriots back in Week 3 of the 2026 season. Armstead was the only Jaguars or Ravens player who was fined for their Week 9 play. Armstead, who signed with the Jaguars in 2024 after spending the first nine years of his career with the 49ers, has 14 tackles, 1.5 sacks and a pass breakup for the Jags this season. Armstead had two tackles in the Jaguars’ 33-10 victory, including the one he was fined for against the Joe Fagnano-led Ravens in Week 9. The funds the NFL collects through fines are donated to the NFLPA’s assistance to retired players, and the NFL Foundation and other nonprofit organizations that support kids’ sports leagues, community wellness initiatives, and the safety, health and well being of athletes at all levels of sports.

item.title: A player's 8-touchdown night fuels big upset in Bay Area HS football playoffs
item.description: A football sits on the sidelines before a high school game in Cumru, Pa., Oct. 9, 2020. (Ben Hasty/Reading Eagle/MediaNews Group via Getty Images) A massive high school football playoff upset in the Bay Area was punctuated by one of the most incredible individual performances in Northern California history. In the North Coast Section (NCS) Division 1 quarterfinals, No. 6 seed Acalanes pulled off the shocking win over No. 3 Pittsburg, winning 70-54 in a video game-like shootout. The game featured a ridiculous 1,200-plus yards of total offense and 18 touchdowns, but it's Dons quarterback Tyler Winkles' performance that will be the talk of the weekend. Winkles' final stat-line included 607 total yards - 471 passing yards and 136 rush yards -- and eight touchdowns. He also threw for two 2-point conversions. The 607 total yards is a North Coast Section record for most yards by a quarterback who also rushed for 100 yards in the same game, according to Cal-Hi Sports' Mark Tennis . Winkles, who is a senior, has no football scholarship offers and as a result, has committed to play baseball at Washington State, according to Bay Area News Group . "The baffling part is every college in the nation not offering him," Acalanes head coach Joel Isaac told Bay Area News Group. "I don't know what people are doing. Best athlete on the field every night." Winkles' record performance is all the more impressive when you take into account that he did it against a Pittsburg defense that features multiple D-I college prospects, notably edge rusher Terrance Murphy , who is committed to Fresno State, and safety Jeremiah Edwards , who's weighing offers from Cal, Oregon State, Washington State and Arizona. "All the other people are going to think it's an upset, but we knew," Winkles told Bay Area News Group after the game. "We were confident going into this game, I promise you that. This game made history for our school, but it's not over. We're still writing the chapters to our story." For Pittsburg, the loss ends the program's five-year reign as NCS Division I champions. It's also the Pirates' first playoff loss to a program not named De La Salle since 2016. Acalanes advances to the Division I semifinals for the second consecutive year, and will face No. 4-seeded San Ramon Valley next Friday. item.title: Michael Pittman Jr. says he feels healthy enough to return
item.description: Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers made no trades ahead of Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline, despite a clear need at wide receiver. Although the Steelers were interested in Tennessee’s Calvin Ridley and Jacksonville’s Brian Thomas Jr., a trade never materialized. While the receiver room has a bleak outlook right now, one of the Steelers’ highest paid receivers seems close to making his return from injured reserve. Steelers veteran wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. has been out since Week 4 after suffering a plantar fasciitis injury. Still, it seems like his return could come sooner rather than later. “It feels good, and today was probably my best day yet,” Pittman told Brendan Howe of Steelers Now on Thursday. “Yesterday was good, today was even better, so definitely trending the right way.… I would love the opportunity to play this week, but that’s out of my control. I definitely let them know today that I thought it was good.” Pittman Jr. remains on injured reserve, with the Steelers yet to open his 21-day practice window. The receiver was seen working off to the side this week and even ran during warmups. Although Pittman Jr. will be out this week against Cincinnati, the receiver feels healthy enough to go. The Steelers acquired Pittman Jr. in a trade with the Indianapolis Colts this past March. item.title: Aston Villa Block Chelsea And Inter Raid On French Star: Is He Untouchable?
item.description: Aston Villa Block Chelsea And Inter Raid On French Star: Is He Untouchable? Aston Villa have told suitors that Boubacar Kamara is not for sale in January or beyond, according to Football Insider. Former Villa scout Mick Brown says Unai Emery treats the 26-year-old France international as a guaranteed starter and has no intention of weakening a midfield that is already short of options. Chelsea , Inter Milan and Saudi Pro League clubs have all been linked with him, yet Brown insists none of them will get a hearing. Why Villa have no choice Amadou Onana tore his cruciate ligament in July, and FotMob lists mid-April 2027 as his expected return, so the player best suited to work alongside Kamara will miss almost the whole season. Brown also claims Villa are trying to extend Ross Barkley’s stay. The 32-year-old has a long record of fitness setbacks, so he works as cover rather than a replacement. What Kamara gives Emery Kamara rarely makes highlight reels, but he keeps Villa’s shape together. FotMob credits him with 28 tackles, 56% of his duels won and 86.3% pass accuracy across 883 Premier League minutes this season. He can also drop into central defence, which Emery has needed before. The weaknesses are just as clear. He hasn’t scored, has managed only 0.14 expected goals from three shots and offers little in the final third. His body has let him down too, with a cruciate injury in February 2024 and a hamstring problem at the start of last season. Should Aston Villa treat Kamara as untouchable? MANCHESTER, ENGLAND – NOVEMBER 08: Boubacar Kamara of Aston Villa reacts after the Premier League 2026/27 match between Manchester United and Aston Villa FC at Old Trafford on November 08, 2026 in Manchester, England. (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images) Yes, and the reasoning is about this season rather than sentiment. Villa conceded three against Barcelona and four at Manchester United in their last two games. A team leaking goals like that cannot sell the one midfielder who protects their back line, least of all when Onana is out, and no January signing at Kamara’s level is likely to be affordable. His contract runs to 2030, so Villa face no pressure to cash in. If a huge bid arrives next summer, with Onana back and fit, the conversation changes. The real worry is cover. Kamara contributes almost nothing going forward, so Emery needs John McGinn, now 32, to provide the creativity next to him. Villa should use January to add one more holding midfielder, even on loan, rather than rely on Barkley’s body staying intact.

item.title: Real Madrid sees Arsenal man as the profile they need to sign in January
item.description: Real Madrid sees Arsenal man as the profile they need to sign in January Martin Zubimendi remains firmly on Real Madrid’s radar as the Spanish giants consider trying to sign him from Arsenal in one of the upcoming transfer windows. Madrid have followed the midfielder since his time at Real Sociedad, but Arsenal won the race for his signature after the Spanish club decided against acting on a recommendation from their manager at the time, Xabi Alonso. Alonso now manages Chelsea and is also interested in bringing Zubimendi to the Premier League club . However, the midfielder could favour a return to Spain with Real Madrid rather than making another move within English football. Although Zubimendi is no longer a regular starter at Arsenal, the Gunners still regard him as one of their most important players. They want to keep him beyond this season and are unlikely to welcome interest from other clubs. Real Madrid identify Zubimendi as midfield target Madrid are aware of Arsenal’s position, but that has not stopped them from considering a move. According to Fichajes , the club have identified Zubimendi as the player who could address their midfield problems and provide the missing link between their defence and attack. The Spanish giants believe his qualities could improve their options in the middle of the pitch. Despite their recent performances under Jose Mourinho, they remain interested in adding another midfielder to their squad, with Zubimendi reportedly at the top of their list. His experience in Spanish football and understanding of the demands of the game in La Liga could make him an attractive option for Madrid as they assess their recruitment plans. (Photo by Jack Thomas/Getty Images) January approach remains possible Real Madrid would ideally prefer to wait until the end of the season before making a move for the Arsenal midfielder. However, there is a possibility that they could approach the Gunners in January. Zubimendi’s limited playing time at Arsenal could encourage Madrid to test the club’s resolve sooner rather than later. They may believe the situation gives them an opportunity to convince him to consider a return to Spain. Arsenal, however, still value the midfielder highly and want him to remain part of their plans. item.title: Comeback kid Joseph thrills as England eye All Blacks
item.description: Eddie Jones aired a complaint about Twickenham's in-stadium experience when he appeared on BBC Radio 5 Live this week. "Being a spectator and being told when to make noise is a bit funny," said the Japan boss, objecting to a big-screen request for an increase in volume. Jones sat stony-faced in the coaching box as the message appeared again in the midst of his team's 78-15 thrashing at England's hands on Saturday. There was little for him to enjoy on his return to Twickenham, where he was head coach for seven years. But, for the rest of a capacity crowd, it was a fun one. With junior tickets on sale at £15, there was a different atmosphere from usual. The decibels were higher, the demographic was younger, the spirits a little lighter. And England brought plenty of entertainment to the party. Thirteen tries in total, with Will Joseph's five putting him in the centre of the chorus line. The 24-year-old won his only previous England cap under Jones. Back in the summer of 2022, he was a teenage apprentice taken on tour to Australia and thrust into the second Test as a last-minute replacement. His promise has taken some time to be fulfilled. He struggled for game time and fitness at Harlequins after London Irish's bankruptcy forced him to move on from his boyhood club. An auto-immune condition that cost him the hearing in his left ear was one setback at the Stoop. But, as part of a rat pack of exciting young English-qualified backs at Gloucester this season, he has been superb: a swerving, offloading, game-breaking threat either on the wing or in midfield. England deployed him out wide, to bring some of the razzle-dazzle that they lost as Immanuel Feyi-Waboso limped out of their autumn campaign. Reports from Pennyhill Park during the week had suggested Joseph was doing a fine job of replicating Feyi-Waboso's explosive elusiveness. He certainly did on Twickenham's main stage, finishing chances with the same pace and power. "He is pretty similar to Immanuel Feyi-Waboso in the way he plays his game," said former England wing Chris Ashton on BBC Radio 5 Live. "He is just so fast. He doesn't look too fast in the first two steps and then he is just gone. He gets away from people." Joseph's cartwheeling plant of the ball over the line for his fourth summed up his exuberance. In the aftermath of that score, Japan flanker Ben Gunter put a consoling arm around full-back Kazuma Ueda, who had been comprehensively burned in a race to the corner. Japan couldn't get near Joseph, whose first try came after just 60 seconds and his hat-trick score in the 19th minute. "It has been a challenging four years, but I have enjoyed the journey to get back here and I am happy all that hard work I have put in has paid off," he said. "I have had a taste for it now and I can't wait to do it again." We have been here before though. There was another teenage apprentice taken on that tour of Australia alongside Joseph. item.title: 'No racism in Spain' – De la Fuente message for Tuchel
item.description: Luis de la Fuente agreed a contract extension in September to stay as Spain boss until 2032 [Getty Images] Luis de la Fuente has dismissed concerns over racism in Spanish football before the national team's Uefa Nations League meeting with England in Madrid on Sunday. Three Lions boss Thomas Tuchel had earlier confirmed he would remind his players of Uefa's anti-racism protocol before the fixture, which will determine who finishes top of League A Group 3. While he has stressed he didn't expect there to be any incidents, the visit will be England's first to the Spanish capital since a notorious 2004 encounter at the Bernabeu was overshadowed by racist chanting directed at their players. Spain head coach De la Fuente was asked whether Tuchel's message to his players showed there was still work needed to tackle racism in Spain. But he responded: "What I'd tell you, and you can tell Thomas, is that in Spain, there's no racism. "Just like that, crystal clear. Just like in England, there's no racism in Spain. We aren't racist, any of us." The Spanish Football Federation was fined last month and ordered to partially close a stadium after supporters directed Islamophobic and xenophobic chants towards Muslims during a match against Egypt in Barcelona. In the domestic game, Real Madrid's Brazilian forward Vinicius Jr has been a vocal anti-racism campaigner after frequently being on the end of racist chanting - and worse. In 2024 three Valencia fans were sentenced to eight months in prison for abusing him at a match. Uefa operates a three-step protocol, allowing referees to stop matches, take players off the pitch temporarily and, ultimately, abandon a game if discriminatory behaviour continues. Tuchel said on Friday: "Maybe we take our five minutes to inform the players about the protocol if there is a precedent [in Madrid]. And then, yeah, we will give our answers if stuff like this happens. Best answers are on the pitch." However, when asked again about his views at a pre-match news conference on Saturday, Tuchel added: "I never talk about racism in Spain. "I answered politely a question about what happens, I never expect racism. I got asked, 'what will happen if and if and if?'. And I said, 'if it happens, there's a protocol in place'. That's it. "But my trust is that we have a friendly atmosphere, that we have an atmosphere who is clearly in favour of the Spanish team, and that football does what it does best: brings people together and not divide people." Midfielder Declan Rice said: "In the past, I've experienced that in Montenegro and Bulgaria and there was a protocol in place that we followed - we came off the pitch. We know exactly where we are as a group on that. "The times we are in now, 2026, there should never be racism in football. It's shocking we still have it in the game today. item.title: Valley Central football got into the Section 9 Class AA final by forfeit. Then, the Vikings won it.
item.description: The Valley Central football team beat Newburgh Free Academy for the Section 9 Class AA title on Saturday. (Jim Franco/Times Union) The Valley Central football team, which was inserted into the Section 9 Class AA championship game after previously undefeated Middletown was forced to forfeit its semifinal victory against it due to the use of an ineligible player, won the sectional final Saturday afternoon in a stunning upset. Valley Central, which entered Saturday's Class AA final against Newburgh Free Academy at Monroe-Woodbury High School with a 5-5 record, came away with a shocking 16-6 win to earn a berth in the state tournament. The Vikings were originally eliminated from the Section 9 playoffs last weekend with a 48-15 loss to Middletown. But, in the days following the game, it emerged that Middletown had used an ineligible player - a soccer player who was used as a kickoff specialist - in that semifinal win and would be forced to forfeit. The decision led to a hasty appeals process and an eventual petition for emergency relief in state Supreme Court that was withdrawn Friday. State rules require an athlete to be an eligible participant for a minimum of three regular-season football games in order to be eligible for postseason play. The player, according to court documents, only played in one regular-season game and was on the sideline for another before he participated in the semifinal game. The Middletown school district appealed to both Section 9 and the New York State Public High School Athletic Association to overturn the decision, but was rejected on both occasions. The district then went to court seeking to have the team's place in the sectional final restored, but the petition was withdrawn following a Friday afternoon hearing. Valley Central will play the winner of Saturday's Section 2 Class AA Super Bowl between Saratoga Springs and Christian Brothers Academy in a state quarterfinal on Nov. 21 at Colonie High School. Elsewhere in the state, a similar situation has affected the Section 4 Class D championship game. Delaware Academy, the No. 2-ranked Class D team in the state, was forced to forfeit its semifinal victory over Deposit/Hancock due to the same rule that led to Middletown's forfeit. Delaware Academy also appealed to its section and NYSPHSAA, which was ultimately unsuccessful. Deposit/Hancock will face Tioga for the Section 4 Class D title on Sunday. item.title: Cam Collier, Carlos Sanchez lead Reds prospects in need of Rule 5 protection
item.description: KNOXVILLE, TN - SEPTEMBER 03: Cam Collier #6 of the Chattanooga Lookouts celebrates in the dugout during the game between the Chattanooga Lookouts and the Knoxville Smokies at Covenant Health Park on Thursday, September 3, 2026 in Knoxville, Tennessee. (Photo by Ryan Beatty/Minor League Baseball via Getty Images) Tuesday, November 17th at 6:00 PM ET marks the deadline for all 30 MLB clubs to add players to their respective 40-man rosters in order to keep them protected from selection in December’s Rule 5 Draft. Said draft, you’ll recall, is a way of preventing teams from hoarding their best and brightest prospects in the minor leagues while blocking their paths for promotion, a field-leveling administrative mechanism that at least gives a little bet of help balancing the power of the 30 individual franchises. As MLB Pipeline noted, there are four current minor leaguers who have been in the franchise long enough to be eligible for Rule 5 selection that also find themselves ranked among the Top 30 within the Cincinnati Reds system. That list is headlined by former 1st round pick Cam Collier as well as Carlos Sanchez, who excelled during the 2026 regular season before bursting even further onto the scene by slashing .300/.425/.571 (.997 OPS) in 20 games in Arizona Fall League play. 1B Carter Graham, who knocked the stitches out of baseballs throughout his own breakout 2026 season, also joins them, as does fellow former 1st round pick Jay Allen II. There are two important caveats worth noting regarding the Rule 5 Draft. Any team that selects a player must keep said player on their active roster for the entire season lest they be forced to offer them back to their original franchise; that means that even though an eligible player may well be uber-talented, they aren’t necessarily going to get picked if they aren’t actually ready for big league play just yet. The other caveat is 2026 specific, as the Rule 5 Draft is scheduled for December 9th during the Winter Meetings…but that’s after the expiration of the current Collective Bargaining Agreement is set to expire on December 1st. It remains to be seen just how much that will impact all the usual administrative deadlines and procedures we see during typical MLB offseasons, and there’s a chance the draft itself gets kicked much further down the road altogether. As for the Reds in particular, they have 37 players currently on their 40-man roster after adding back players who finished the regular season on the 60-day IL. So, if they’re to actually protect all four of the players listed above (and/or anyone else that’s eligible and not one of MLB Pipeline’s Top 30 prospects in the system) they’re going to have to remove someone who’s currently holding a spot. We’ll find out more come Tuesday!

item.title: Ohio State defeats Northwestern 28-19, but has anything changed?
item.description: COLUMBUS, OH - NOVEMBER 14: Ohio State Buckeyes wide receiver Jeremiah Smith #4 catches a pass during the first quarter of the game between the Ohio State Buckeyes and the Northwestern Wildcats at Ohio Stadium in Columbus, Ohio on November 14, 2026. (Photo by Jason Mowry/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Ohio State ended its two-game skid on Saturday, knocking off Northwestern 28-19. Winning games is obviously better than losing games, and you have to give credit to the Buckeyes for fighting through another rough performance and ultimately earning the victory. That said, this latest outing didn’t do a whole lot to quiet the doubters or show that Ohio State has learned from its mistakes. While Ohio State emerged victorious, it felt like they did so largely as a result of a gap in talent between the two sides. Ryan Day and his staff did very little to actually correct the issues that have plagued the Buckeyes in those prior two losses, even despite the final outcome. One of the most glaring problems is Matt Patricia’s third down defense, which was again mostly dreadful against Northwestern. Facing a team starting its backup quarterback, and lacking the supposed QB depth of a program like Ohio State, the Wildcats still managed to convert on 6-of-11 third downs through the game’s first three quarters. It wasn’t as if Northwestern was facing third-and-short either, as their average third down distance to go was 8.5 yards. Of the seven big plays Ohio State allowed (passes of 15+ yards or runs of 10+ yards), four of them came on third or fourth down. The Buckeyes twice allowed passing plays of 20+ yards on third-and-long, and also gave up a 10-yard run on a third-and-2 late in the second quarter. After doing a great job of limiting those explosive plays over the first six weeks of the season, Ohio State is now regularly allowing big chunk yardage — and mostly on third down. Patricia did go away from the three-man rushes that have doomed the Buckeyes’ defense in those spots in their prior two games, but they remained unable to get off the field in big spots time and time again. The most highly paid defensive coordinator in the country has not nearly earned his paycheck this season. Ohio State is routinely getting out-leveraged with too many players stacked to one side, and the middle of the field has been wide open more often than not. On the other hand, the Buckeyes’ pass rush was significantly improved in this game, as the Silver Bullets racked up five sacks against the Wildcats. Will Smith Jr.‘s first quarter sack broke a streak of five-straight games (!!) without a single sack from an Ohio State defensive lineman. Kenyatta Jackson led the team with two sacks, the first multi-sack game for a Buckeye this season. Qua Russaw and James Smith also added one sack apiece. item.title: Cowboys’ George Pickens Gets Eye-Opening $136 Million Prediction
item.description: George Pickens #3 of the Dallas Cowboys Getty It is advisable for NFL players, especially teammates like George Pickens and CeeDee Lamb of the Dallas Cowboys, to not cast their eyes toward the paychecks of others. The market can be a fickle thing, and sometimes timing counts for more than talent or merit. But Pickens is a pending NFL free agent after having signed a one-year, $27.3 million franchise tag in the offseason, and though he has done well to not discuss his finances much, and to avoid looking ahead to free agency, there is no doubt that every catch he makes, every number he posts, has an impact on what he will be paid in four months or so. When the season began, with Pickens coming off a massive 93-catch, 1,429-yard season in Dallas, there was speculation that he could demand a contract in the range of what top-paid receiver Jaxson Smith-Njigba received, four years and $168.6 million–or $42.2 million per year. Pickens has not played to that level, but that does not change the fact that he plays a premium position, and is likely to be paid a premium contract. How High Would the Cowboys Go? Whether the Cowboys will pay that deal is a fair question. They’ve already got Lamb on a four-year, $136 million contract, and though Lamb is obviously the superior receiver, the folks at Bleacher Report say that Pickens is likely to get a similar contract. In sussing out what Pickens might get paid, the site listed Lamb ($34 million AAV), Zay Flowers ($35 million) or Garrett Wilson ($32.5 million) as comps. The site pegs Pickens as the No. 2 overall free agent in this winter’s class, and that will drive up his value. It is unlikely that, if the market on Pickens gets that high, the Cowboys would stay involved in re-signing him. George Pickens a Top FA Target From Bleacher Report , where fellow Cowboys star Joey Porter Jr. is also listed as a top 2027 free agent: “George Pickens might not be the top wide receiver available on the 2027 market, but that won’t prevent him from being the top target for a lot of teams. He’s been an elite No. 2 receiver for the Dallas Cowboys. He will only turn 26 in March. … “With a great blend of speed, size (6’3″, 200 lbs), and contested-catch ability, Pickens should heavily interest teams that need a go-to target and don’t want to dish out a market-topping contract. On the open market, he should fall somewhere in the range of Lamb, Garrett Wilson, and Zay Flowers.” This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Cowboys’ George Pickens Gets Eye-Opening $136 Million Prediction appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Ex-Commanders Draft Bust Named Midseason NFL All-Pro
item.description: Washington Commanders edge rusher Chase Young. Getty You won’t find anyone from the Washington Commanders on any midseason awards lists or midseason NFL All-Pro Teams. You will, however, find several former Commanders, including their 2020 No. 2 overall pick, edge rusher Chase Young, who was named to the midseason NFL All-Pro Team by ESPN’s Bill Barnwell. Through 8 games with the New Orleans Saints, Young has 8.0 sacks, 5 TFL, 13 QB hits, 4 pass deflections, 1 forced fumble, and 1 fumble recovery. All of this comes after he had a career-high 10.0 sacks in 2025 for the Saints in just 12 games and 5.0 sacks in his first season with the Saints in 2024, when he played in all 17 regular-season games for the first time in his career but made zero starts. “I never felt like somebody could block me,” Young told NOF Network on November 12. “My first year with the Saints, when I was top ten in pressures, I wasn’t landing the sacks, but I was winning.” Young was one of two elite edge rushers the Commanders traded away midway through the 2023 season — Young to the San Francisco 49ers and Montez Sweat to the Chicago Bears. Young Headed Toward Massive Payday in 2027 Bleacher Report’s Gary Davenport called Young’s next big-money deal 1 of the NFL’s “Most Important Contract Decisions” in 2026. Young signed a 3-year, $51 million contract with the Saints in March 2025. “Last year, it finally came together for Saints edge-rusher Chase Young,” Davenport wrote on August 2. “It didn’t look like it was going to — the former No. 2 overall pick missed the season’s first five games with a calf injury. But once Young was back on the field, he caught fire—a career-high 10 sacks in 12 games … Young is under contract through 2027 at a bargain price relative to what other high-end edge-rushers make. If he can back up last year’s numbers with a hot start in 2026, extending the 27-year-old now could save the Saints a boatload of scratch down the road.” Chase Young’s Disastrous Time With Commanders Young started his career like a man on fire, winning NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year and helping lead the Commanders to the playoffs in 2020 with 44 tackles, 7.5 sacks, 10 TFL, 4 forced fumbles, 1 fumble recovery, 4 pass deflections, and 1 defensive touchdown. He became part of an incredible run of 1st-round picks who didn’t pan out for the Commanders — 6 picks in 5 years from 2019 to 2023 no longer on their roster by the end of the 2024 season. Mallory scored three times in the 36-25 win. ©Marta Lavandier MIAMI GARDENS — Darian Mensah passed for 382 yards and a touchdown against his former school, Javian Mallory scored three times and No. 5 Miami moved closer to wrapping up a trip to the Atlantic Coast Conference title game by beating Duke 36-25 on Saturday. Mark Fletcher Jr. also rushed for a score for Miami (9-1, 7-0 ACC, No. 7 College Football Playoff), which tied a school mark with its 11th consecutive ACC victory. Cooper Barkate — like Mensah, a former Duke star — had his first 100-yard game for Miami, catching eight passes for 134 yards. Mensah, who transferred to Miami after leading Duke to last season’s ACC title, completed 30 of 41 passes for Miami and went over the 3,000-yard mark for the season. Nate Sheppard accounted for 240 yards — 131 rushing, 93 receiving and 16 passing — plus rushed for two scores and caught a conversion pass for Duke (7-3, 4-3). Sheppard had a pair of 47-yard runs in the game, along with 12 catches. Walker Eget completed 26 of 42 passes for 195 yards and a touchdown for the Blue Devils but was intercepted by Miami’s Xavier Lucas with 6:54 left. Mallory’s 39-yard touchdown run on the ensuing possession sealed the win for Miami. Miami’s win, combined with Wake Forest’s victory over SMU, put the Hurricanes on the cusp of clinching a spot in the ACC title game. The Hurricanes would wrap up a berth in the Dec. 5 contest if North Carolina beats Louisville later Saturday night; otherwise, Miami needs only one win in its final two games to clinch. Duke never led, but Miami was never comfortably up until the final minutes. Fletcher — who didn’t get a carry in the second half, evidently because of some sort of injury — had a scoring run midway through the second quarter to put Miami up 10-3. It was the first touchdown allowed by Duke in its last 210 defensive snaps, spanning 36 possessions over 13 quarters. The Blue Devils forced 18 punts, stopped six drives on downs, had four takeaways and had opponents go 5 for 7 on field goal tries in that span. Sheppard tied it for Duke with one of the 47-yard runs on the next possession, before Miami settled on a 13-10 lead at the half. Mallory and Mensah connected to break it open for Miami in the third with a 63-yard catch-and-run to make it 22-10. Sheppard scored again to get Duke within five, but Mallory scored twice in a span of 3:45 midway through the fourth quarter to make it 36-17. The takeaway Duke: Sheppard became the first Duke player with two runs of 40 yards or more in an ACC game since Daniel Jones — the No. 6 pick in the 2019 draft and current Indianapolis Colts quarterback — had runs of 61 and 68 yards in a 42-35 win over North Carolina on Nov. 10, 2018. item.title: Instant reactions to Alabama's Week 11 road win vs. Vanderbilt
item.description: On Saturday afternoon, the Alabama Crimson Tide traveled to Nashville for their first game inside FirstBank Stadium since being upset by Vanderbilt back in 2024. Ultimately, it was Alabama getting back in the win column in Nashville by defeating the Commodores , 21-6. Not all was positive though for the Crimson Tide, as Alabama certainly saw their fair share of struggles, especially during the first half offensively. The Crimson Tide owned a slim 7-3 lead at halftime, with that lone first half touchdown not coming until the final seconds of the second quarter. Alabama then pulled away in the third quarter, and used some big defensive stops late to secure the win. Let's take a look at some instant reactions to Alabama's road win at Vanderbilt. Alabama's defense dominates Vanderbilt offense To keep it simple, Alabama's defense was dominant Saturday in Nashville. Overall, the Crimson Tide held Vanderbilt to only 235 yards of total offense, and did not allow a touchdown to the Commodores. Alabama also held Vanderbilt to 2-of-15 on third downs, as well as 1-of-4 on fourth. The Tide also had five sacks and nine TFL as a team. Keelon Russell starts at quarterback The status of Alabama starting quarterback Keelon Russell had been in question all week leading up to kickoff, but it was the sophomore under center for the Tide on Saturday. Russell ended up playing the entire game completing 22-of-33 passes for 217 yards and three touchdowns. The sophomore also had an interception, as well as a fumble. Daniel Hill has big showing in run game One of the bright spots Saturday for Alabama on offense was running back Daniel Hill, who ended up with one of his best performances of the season up to this point. Receiving a vast majority of Alabama's carries, Hill rushed for 89 yards on 14 attempts, averaging 6.4 yards per carry. Alabama keeps CFP, SEC title hopes alive With the win at Vanderbilt, Alabama continues to inch closer to securing not only a potential College Football Playoff berth, but also a potential trip to Atlanta for the SEC Championship Game. The Crimson Tide (8-2 overall, 6-2 SEC) have two games remaining on their regular season schedule at home against Chattanooga and Auburn.
